faq.q: Why is the fire bell so loud?
faq.a: It is loud so every person in the whole building can hear it. You can cover your ears or wear ear defenders if your school says yes.
asks: Tell me about The bell rings

faq.a: No, bags and things stay inside. Leaving them helps everyone get out quickly. They will be there when you come back.
asks: Tell me about I leave behind

faq.q: Why do we have fire drills?
faq.a: A drill is practice. It helps everyone learn what to do. Then they can stay calm and safe if there is ever a real fire.

faq.q: What if I feel scared in a fire drill?
faq.a: Stay close to your teacher and follow the line. You can hold a friend's hand. A grown-up you trust can tell you before a drill, if they know.

faq.q: Can I know when a drill is coming?
faq.a: Sometimes. You can ask your teacher, Can you tell me before a drill, please? Some schools can do that.

facts: Schools practise fire drills so everyone knows how to leave the building safely.
In a fire drill, people walk, not run, and leave their things behind.

quiz.say: The drill bell rings in Zainab's class. What does she do?
quiz.show: 🔔 The bell rings. What does Zainab do?

options.show: Run as fast as she can
options.say: Run as fast as she can

quiz.why: Lining up and walking with her class keeps everyone safe. Her teacher knows where everyone is.

wrong.0: Running can make people trip, so walking is safer.
wrong.1: In a fire drill, everyone goes outside with the teacher.

quiz.say: The drill bell rings. What happens to Tom's bag?
quiz.show: 🎒 The bell rings. What about Tom's bag?

options.show: Tom gives it to a friend
options.say: Tom gives it to a friend

quiz.why: Bags stay inside so everyone can walk out quickly. The bag will be there later.

wrong.1: Carrying a bag slows Tom down in the line.
wrong.2: His friend leaves things behind too.
